finding: The study provides novel reference ranges for blood pressure immediately after birth in term and preterm infants, finding that preterm infants who were female, born vaginally, had delayed cord clamping, and did not require positive pressure ventilation or develop brain injury had significantly higher SBP, DBP, and MBP at some measurement points within the first hour after birth.
mod_finding: Preterm infants born vaginally had significantly higher SBP, DBP, and MBP at some measurement points within the first hour after birth.
gest_age: Term and preterm (30 weeks mean gestation for preterm infants)
birth_weight: Term infants: 3298 g (mean), Preterm infants: 1340 g (mean)
